lines: +# Alchemy: Cloudflare resource coverage, per-PR stages, state, local dev and tests
+Research for issue #8 (map #1). Checked 2026-11-07.
+## Version researched
+- **`alchemy@2.0.0-beta.85`** (npm `latest` tag, released 2026-11-02) together with **`@alchemy.run/cloudflare@2.0.0-beta.85`**. Source checked at `alchemy-run/alchemy@d096cad` (2026-11-06).
+  - npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/alchemy
+  - Release: https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/releases/tag/v2.0.0-beta.85
+- **Read this first.** Alchemy now has two lines. Most older blog posts and examples describe v1.

+  - **v2 ("Infrastructure as Effects")** lives at https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy, with docs at https://alchemy.run. The stack is an `Alchemy.Stack(...)` built from `Effect.gen` programs, and each cloud is its own package (`@alchemy.run/cloudflare`, `@alchemy.run/github`, ...). It requires **Effect 4** (`effect ^4.1.0`, see `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog). v2 is still in **beta**, but npm `latest` points at it.

+  - **v1 (async/await)** has moved to https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy-async. `github.com/sam-goodwin/alchemy` now redirects there. Its last release is `v0.94.0` (2026-08-01), with docs at https://v1.alchemy.run. Migration guide: https://alchemy.run/migrating-from-v1

+- SPEC §6 picks Effect for all logic, so v2 fits well. Resources, bindings and runtime clients share one Effect program, and the bindings are typed Effect services. **Recommendation: build on v2, pin an exact beta version, and expect breaking changes between betas.**
+Below, "src:" links point to `https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/d096cad7e5506a57aa829dad97079eb94ff4af08/packages/cloudflare/src/...` (written as `cf/...`).
+## 1. Resource coverage (v2)
+| SPEC need | Supported? | Alchemy API | Notes / gaps | Sources |

+| Worker + static assets (one Worker for API + SPA) | Yes | `Cloudflare.Worker(id, { main, assets })`. `assets` takes a directory or a config with `notFoundHandling: "single-page-application"`, `runWorkerFirst: ["/api/*"]` and `htmlHandling`. You can also use `Cloudflare.Website.Vite(...)`, which runs your Vite build and uploads the client output as Worker assets. | With an SPA fallback, set `runWorkerFirst: ["/api/*"]` so API routes reliably reach the Worker. `Website.Vite` treats the SSR bundle as the Worker entry. If you want a plain SPA plus an Effect API Worker, use `Worker` + `assets` and build Vite yourself, or check that `Website.Vite`'s inherited Worker props fit. No `wrangler.jsonc` is needed. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/workers (section "Serve static assets"), https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/vite, src: `cf/Workers/Assets.ts` |

+| Durable Objects, SQLite storage | Yes | `Cloudflare.DurableObject<T>()("Name", Effect.gen(...))`. Methods it returns become typed RPC. `Cloudflare.DurableObjectState` gives `storage` (KV and SQL). | **New DO classes default to SQLite.** The provider emits `new_sqlite_classes` (src: `cf/Workers/WorkerProvider.ts` ~L3752, "Default all new Durable Object classes to SQLite"). Classes are deployed with Cloudflare's declarative **`exports`** map. Wrangler uses the same flow since 4.107, and you **cannot go back** to the old `migrations` flow afterwards. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/durable-objects |

+| DO class migrations (add / delete / rename / transfer) | Yes, mostly automatic | Added classes are created as SQLite. Removed classes become `deleted_classes`. Moving a class to another Worker uses `transferredFrom: "<old script>"` (emits `transferred_classes`). | If a namespace's class is no longer exported, **the deploy stops** instead of silently deleting data. Export the class again, or delete it on purpose. Open issue #2976 says a "rename upload exceeds Cloudflare's 100-entry exports limit" (seen in Alchemy's Domain package). | src: `cf/Workers/WorkerProvider.ts` (L81–116, L3152–3161), https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/durable-objects (section "Adopt a Worker deployed by Wrangler"), https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/issues/2976 |

+| DO SQL schema migrations (inside each object) | Yes | `const m = yield* Cloudflare.SqlMigrations("./drizzle")` in the outer Effect, then `yield* m.apply()` in the inner Effect. Pending SQL runs when each object activates, before its methods are available. Works with Drizzle (`Drizzle.DurableObject({ migrations })`) and Effect SQL. | This is the per-tenant schema migration path SPEC §6.2 needs, and Alchemy provides it. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/durable-objects (section "SQL migrations"), https://alchemy.run/sql/effect-sql/migrations, src: `cf/Workers/SqlMigrations*.ts` |

+| D1 (global index) | Yes | `Cloudflare.D1.Database("Db", { migrations: "./migrations", primaryLocationHint, jurisdiction, readReplication })`. Bind with `D1.QueryDatabase`. `SQL.D1(d1)` gives an Effect `SqlClient`. | Migrations are applied **on every deploy**, in numeric-prefix order, and tracked in `__alchemy_migrations`. Databases already migrated with wrangler or drizzle-kit are picked up where they left off. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/d1, https://alchemy.run/sql/effect-sql/d1 |

+| Workflows (round lifecycle) | Yes | `Cloudflare.Workflow<T>()("Name", Effect.gen(... Effect.fn(input => ...)))`. Durable steps use `Cloudflare.Workflows.task(name, effect, { retries, timeout, rollback })` and sleeps. Workflows also take native `schedules: ["0 * * * *"]`. | A second engine (`DurableObjectEngine`) runs `effect/workflow` on Durable Objects. This is an alternative, not required. Open issues: #2776 (per-Activity `step.do` retries and timeout are not exposed on `NativeEngine` for `effect/workflow`) and #2801 (the DO engine's sequential sleeps inherit alarm backoff). The native `Cloudflare.Workflow` + `task` path is the simplest one. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/workflows, https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/effect-workflows, src: `cf/Workflows/` |

+| Queues + consumers + DLQ | Yes | `Cloudflare.Queues.Queue("Q")`, `Cloudflare.Queues.Consumer(id, { queueId, deadLetterQueue: dlq.queueName, settings: { maxRetries, maxBatchSize, retryDelay, ... } })`. Producer binding is `WriteQueue`. Effect consumers attach as an event source on the Worker. | The source warns explicitly: "Cloudflare does not drain or alert on a dead-letter queue". **Declare a consumer for the DLQ too**, or dead-lettered messages expire unseen. The DLQ can be a ref to another stack's queue. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/messaging/queues, src: `cf/Queues/Consumer.ts` (L36–175) |

+| Cron Triggers | Yes | `yield* Cloudflare.Workers.cron("0 * * * *", handler)` plus `Effect.provide(Cloudflare.Workers.CronEventSourceLive)`. One call sets the trigger at deploy time and registers the handler at runtime. Async Workers can use a `crons` prop instead. | A failing handler is caught and logged. It does not crash the Worker, so report errors yourself. Workflows can instead use native `schedules`. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/messaging/cron |

+| R2 | Yes | `Cloudflare.R2.Bucket("B", { lifecycle, cors, domains, locks, forceDestroy })`, with `ReadBucket` / `WriteBucket` / `ReadWriteBucket` bindings and presigned URLs. | **Destroying a bucket that still has objects fails** (`BucketNotEmpty`) unless you set `forceDestroy: true`. Set it on PR stages (`stage.startsWith("pr-")`), or PR teardown fails once exports exist. Open issue #2985: drift detection cannot see lifecycle, CORS or domain changes. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/r2, src: `cf/R2/Bucket.ts` (L266–288) |
+| KV | Yes | `Cloudflare.KV.Namespace("Cache")`, with `ReadNamespace` / `WriteNamespace` / `ReadWriteNamespace` bindings. | No gaps found. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/kv |

+| Workers Analytics Engine | Yes | `Cloudflare.AnalyticsEngine.Dataset("Events", { dataset: "app_events" })` + `WriteDataset` binding (`writeDataPoint`). | A dataset is configuration only. Cloudflare creates it on first write. **Alchemy has no query client**, so read metrics through Cloudflare's SQL API over HTTP yourself. In local dev, writes go to a no-op stub. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/observability/analytics-engine, src: `packages/cloudflare-runtime/src/core/bindings/analytics-engine/` |

+| Turnstile | Yes | `Cloudflare.Turnstile.Widget("Answer", { domains, mode: "managed" \| "non-interactive" \| "invisible" })`. Outputs are `sitekey` (public) and `secret` (`Redacted`). | Server-side `siteverify` is your code. Alchemy manages only the widget. For PR stages, `domains` must include the preview hostname (`*.workers.dev` or a preview subdomain). There is no local simulator, so in dev and tests use Cloudflare's published test sitekeys/secrets (https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/troubleshooting/testing/). | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/security/turnstile, src: `cf/Turnstile/Widget.ts` |

+| Cloudflare email sending | Yes (binding + sending domain) | `Cloudflare.Email.SendingSubdomain("Mail", { zoneId, name: "mail.example.com" })` provisions DKIM, SPF and return-path, and creates the DNS records on Cloudflare-hosted zones. `Cloudflare.Email.SendEmail("Email", { allowedSenderAddresses?, allowedDestinationAddresses? })` + `Cloudflare.Email.Send(...)` gives a typed `send({ from, to, subject, text, html })`. Routing, rules and catch-all are covered too. | The `send-and-receive` page still says sending "needs Email Routing enabled", while `SendingSubdomain` points to the newer Email Sending product. Whether the binding can reach arbitrary recipients is a Cloudflare product limit, not an Alchemy one. Settle it in the email-sending research ticket. A sending subdomain carries no ownership marker, so taking over an existing one needs `--adopt`. Local dev writes `.eml` files to `.alchemy/local/email`. To send for real in dev, wrap the binding in `Alchemy.remote()`. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/email, https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/email/send-and-receive, src: `cf/Email/SendingSubdomain.ts`, `cf/Email/SendEmail.ts` |

+| Worker secrets | Yes | `yield* Config.Redacted("WORKOS_API_KEY")` in a Worker's construction phase. It is read at deploy time and bound as `secret_text`. The Stack's `secrets:` option picks the source per stage (`.env`, Doppler, Infisical). `Alchemy.Random` mints stable generated tokens. | Open issue #2800: **a secret dropped from `env` is not deleted** and stays live on the Worker. Issue #2757: secrets written outside Alchemy are lost on upload. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/security/secrets-env, https://alchemy.run/environments/secret-providers, https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/issues/2800 |

+| Secrets Store | Yes | `Cloudflare.SecretsStore.Store("S")` adopts the account's single store and **never deletes it**. Then `Cloudflare.SecretsStore.Secret("X", { store, value, name? })` + `ReadSecret` binding. Values are read live, with no redeploy needed. | **Gap for per-PR stages:** the secret name defaults to the logical ID **with no stage prefix** (`resolveName = (id, name) => name ?? id`, src: `cf/SecretsStore/Secret.ts` L574). Every stage writes into the same account-wide store, so `pr-12` and `prod` would fight over `WORKOS_API_KEY`. Workaround: pass `name: \`${stage}_WORKOS_API_KEY\``, or use plain Worker secrets (`Config.Redacted`) for per-stage values and keep the Secrets Store for values that really are shared. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/security/secrets-store |

+| Custom domains & DNS | Yes | `Cloudflare.Worker(..., { domain: "app.example.com" })` or `{ name, aliases, redirects, previews: true }` creates the DNS record and certificate. `Cloudflare.Zone.Zone` (create or adopt), `Cloudflare.DNS.Record`, `Workers.WorkerRoute`, `Zone.Setting` and `DNS.Dnssec` are also available. | The zone must already be in the account, or declared with `Zone.Zone`. Zones default to the **`retain`** removal policy. DNS records have no local provider, so in `alchemy dev` they deploy to the real cloud into your personal stage. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/networking/custom-domains, https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/networking/domains |

+| AI Gateway | Yes | `Cloudflare.AI.Gateway("Gw", { cacheTtl, rateLimiting*, collectLogs, logManagement, authentication, ... })`. Every prop updates in place. `Cloudflare.AI.QueryGateway(Gw)` returns a typed client and an Effect `LanguageModel` layer. | Logging policy (`collectLogs: false` for raw comments) is a gateway prop, which is what SPEC §6.1 needs. Gateway DLP and guardrail resources also exist (`cf/AI/SecuritySettings.ts`, `CustomTopics.ts`). | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/ai/ai-gateway |

+| Workers AI | Yes | `yield* Cloudflare.Workers.AI()` binds `ai` and returns a client. There is an Effect `LanguageModel` layer, and it can be routed through the gateway. | **No local model.** In dev the binding is a remote binding, so it calls real Cloudflare with your credentials and is billed (src: `packages/cloudflare-runtime/src/core/bindings/Ai.ts` uses `makeRemoteBinding`). Mock the domain `LanguageModel` service in tests. | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/ai/workers-ai |

+| Effect HTTP API on Workers | Yes (bonus) | Docs for Effect `HttpApi` / RPC on Workers and Durable Objects. | Matches SPEC §6.1 "Effect's platform HTTP API module". | https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/apis/effect-http-api |

+Also present but not needed by SPEC: Hyperdrive, Vectorize, AI Search, Containers, Pipelines, Access, Rate limiting, Workers for Platforms, Tunnel and others (src: `packages/cloudflare/src/` directory listing).
+## 2. Stages and per-PR previews

+**Stage model.** A stage is an isolated instance of a Stack, with its own state and its own physical names, for example `myapp-pr_147-photos-9b2c`. If you pass no stage, `alchemy deploy` defaults to `live_$USER`, `alchemy dev` to `dev_$USER`, and tests to `test_$USER`. Names must match `[a-z0-9][-_a-z0-9]*`. The stage is resolved from `--stage`, then `$ALCHEMY_STAGE`, then the default. Code can branch on it with `yield* Stack` → `stack.stage`, for example `RemovalPolicy.retain(stack.stage === "prod")` or `protect`. Sources: https://alchemy.run/environments/stages, src: `packages/alchemy/src/RemovalPolicy.ts`.
+A PR stage gets its own Workers, D1 databases, DO namespaces (because the Worker is separate), queues, buckets and so on. This matches SPEC §6.4 directly.
+**GitHub Actions (official pattern).** https://alchemy.run/environments/ci
+- Trigger on `push: [main]` and `pull_request: [opened, reopened, synchronize, closed]`. Use `concurrency: deploy-${{ github.ref }}` and `cancel-in-progress: false`.
+- `STAGE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.number) || (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'prod' || github.ref_name) }}`

+- The `deploy` job runs `alchemy deploy --stage $STAGE` when the action is not `closed`. The `cleanup` job runs on `closed` and does `alchemy destroy --stage $STAGE`. It includes a safety check that refuses `prod`.
+- A `GitHub.Comment` resource with a stable logical ID posts the preview URL and updates it on each push. It uses `GitHub.GitHubEnv` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `pull-requests: write`.

+- "Credentials as code": a separate `stacks/github.ts` is deployed once with an `admin` profile. It mints a scoped `Cloudflare.ApiToken.AccountApiToken` and writes it to the repo with `GitHub.Secret` / `GitHub.Variable`. Run `alchemy provider check-env` as the first CI step to fail fast.

+- **Composite action:** the repo root has an `action.yml` (`uses: alchemy-run/alchemy@main`, mentioned in the beta-62 blog post). It decides deploy, destroy or skip by itself. Note that it names PR stages **`staging-<n>`**, not `pr-<n>` as the docs do. Pin a SHA if you use it, or just copy the workflow above. Source: https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/d096cad7e5506a57aa829dad97079eb94ff4af08/action.yml

+**Worker Previews (`preview.of`) are a different thing.** They are Cloudflare's per-branch copy of one Worker, with its own URL and its own DO state. However, "Service bindings from a Preview resolve to production; **crons, queue consumers, and production routes stay on production**. For an end-to-end multi-Worker PR, deploy a full stage instead." Because SurveyBeat depends on Workflows, Queues and Cron, **use full stages per PR, not `preview.of`.** Source: https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/previews
+**Teardown gotchas for PR stages:**
+- R2 buckets need `forceDestroy: true`, or a destroy with objects present fails.
+- Secrets Store secrets need stage-specific names (see §1). The store itself is never deleted.
+- Zones are `retain` by default. Keep the zone in a shared stack and give PRs subdomains, or just use `workers.dev`.
+- Turnstile widget domains must cover PR hostnames.

+- Open issue #2921 asks for "destroy several stages in one process". Today there is no built-in sweeper for orphaned `pr-*` stages, for example when a cleanup job failed. Workaround: a scheduled job that runs `alchemy state list` and destroys stages whose PRs are closed. CLI reference: https://alchemy.run/cli/state
+## 3. State in CI
+- **Default:** local files in `.alchemy/state/<stack>/<stage>/*.json`. Gitignore them. This is fine for solo work but useless on ephemeral CI runners.

+- **`Cloudflare.state()` (recommended):** an `alchemy-state-store` Worker in your account, backed by a **Durable Object with embedded SQLite**. State is encrypted at rest with a key, and the bearer token is kept in your **Secrets Store**. The first local run bootstraps it. **In CI (`CI=true`) a missing store fails the run on purpose**, so provision it once with `alchemy state bootstrap --profile <ci-profile>`. In CI, credentials are resolved from the Secrets Store on each run through a short-lived edge-preview Worker, so nothing is persisted. `Cloudflare.state({ workerName })` gives you a separate store. Source: https://alchemy.run/state-store
+  - The test-harness page calls `Cloudflare.state()` "R2-backed". That is outdated. The source (`cf/StateStore/Store.ts`) is a Durable Object.
+  - Open issue #2805: `Cloudflare.state()` cannot use a different account than the Cloudflare providers.
+- Alternatives: `AWS.state()` (DynamoDB), `GCP.state()` (GCS), or a custom store (https://alchemy.run/state-store/custom-state-store).
+## 4. Local dev mode

+- `alchemy dev` (default stage `dev_$USER`) runs Workers in **workerd directly**, with Alchemy's own simulators in `@alchemy.run/cloudflare-runtime`. **It is not Miniflare.** Miniflare appears only in Alchemy's private test tools. SPEC §6.3's "Miniflare, through Alchemy's dev mode" is slightly off: the emulation is workerd-based, but it is not Miniflare. v1 did use Miniflare (`alchemy-async/alchemy/src/cloudflare/miniflare/`). Source: https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/local-development, src: `packages/cloudflare-runtime/package.json` (depends on `workerd`, not `miniflare`).

+- **Emulated locally:** Workers (with hot reload), Durable Objects including SQLite, KV, R2 (plus an S3 endpoint), D1 (migrations applied on every reconcile), Queues + consumers (batching, retry, **dead-letter semantics**), Workflows ("real step semantics"), Secrets Store (seeded with real values), and Vite and other framework dev servers with HMR. Crons fire on schedule, and `/cdn-cgi/handler/scheduled` triggers them manually. Email `send_email` writes `.eml` files, and `POST /cdn-cgi/handler/email` drives inbound mail.
+- **Not emulated:** Workers AI is a remote binding (real calls, billed). Analytics Engine is a no-op stub. Turnstile has no simulator. DNS and Vectorize deploy to the cloud in your personal stage.
+- `Alchemy.remote()` opts a single resource out of emulation, for example a real queue or real email. Moving a resource between local and live plans a **replacement**.

+- Open issues: #2810 (mixing local and remote is hard to get right), #2884 (local R2 S3 credentials are rejected by S3 clients), #2879 (binding clients fail when the env name differs from the logical ID).
+## 5. Vitest integration

+- `@alchemy.run/test` provides `Test.make({ providers, state, stage, dev })` with adapters for `alchemy-test`, `bun test` and **Vitest** (`@alchemy.run/test/Vitest` + `@effect/vitest`, where each test is an `it.live`). `deploy(Stack)` / `destroy(Stack)` run the real stack. **`dev: true` runs it against the local workerd simulators instead of the cloud.** The test stage defaults to `test_$USER`, or set `ALCHEMY_TEST_STAGE=ci-pr-42`. Sources: https://alchemy.run/testing/test-harness, https://alchemy.run/testing/testing-a-stack, https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/tutorial/part-4

+- **Gap:** tests run in Node (or Bun) and drive the stack over HTTP or RPC. This is integration-style testing. Alchemy has **no integration with `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`**: no grep hits in the repo, and no wrangler-config generator in v2 (v1 had `WranglerJson`). To unit-test DO or adapter code inside the isolate (calling `runInDurableObject` or reading storage directly), you would need a separate test-only wrangler config for vitest-pool-workers, which works against SPEC's "no hand-edited wrangler config". **Workaround (recommended):** keep domain logic in plain Node tests, as SPEC already requires. Test the adapters through `Test.make({ dev: true })` against small test-only RPC methods or HTTP routes in the stack. Run a smaller `Test.make()` cloud smoke test on the PR stage.
+## 6. Gaps and workarounds (summary)
+1. **v2 is beta.** Pin an exact version and budget time for API churn. v1 is in maintenance in a separate repo.
+2. **Secrets Store names are not stage-scoped.** Set `name` per stage, or use Worker `secret_text` through `Config.Redacted`.
+3. **R2 PR teardown fails if a bucket is not empty.** Set `forceDestroy` for non-prod stages.
+4. **The DLQ needs its own consumer.** Cloudflare does not alert on dead-lettered messages.
+5. **Worker Previews do not carry crons or queue consumers.** Use full `pr-<n>` stages.
+6. **No stage sweeper.** Add a scheduled cleanup for orphaned PR stages (#2921).
+7. **Dropped Worker secrets linger** (#2800). Rotate or delete them by hand when you remove one.
+8. **Local dev:** Workers AI is remote (billed), Analytics Engine is a stub, and Turnstile has no simulator. Mock `LanguageModel` and use Cloudflare's Turnstile test keys.
+9. **No vitest-pool-workers integration.** Alchemy's Vitest adapter tests deployed or local stacks from Node.
+10. **Analytics Engine queries** are not wrapped by Alchemy. Call Cloudflare's SQL API yourself.
+11. **Email:** Alchemy has the resources, but whether Cloudflare Email Sending can reach arbitrary recipients and how good deliverability is are Cloudflare questions for the email ticket.

+12. Docs disagree with each other in places: the `action.yml` stage name is `staging-<n>` versus `pr-<n>` in the docs, and the test-harness page says the state store is "R2-backed". Trust the source code.
+# Cloudflare Email Service for SurveyBeat transactional email
+Research for issue #6 (map #1). Question: can Cloudflare Email Service send SurveyBeat's Invitations, reminders and results-ready notices from a Worker, and if not, what is the fallback (SPEC §6.1)?
+All sources were read on 2026-11-07. Dates in brackets are the "last updated" date on the page, where shown.
+## Short answer

+Yes, with caveats. Email Sending is in **public beta** since 2026-04-16, on Workers Paid only. It has what SurveyBeat needs: a Worker binding, automatic SPF/DKIM/DMARC, bounce and complaint events delivered to a Cloudflare Queue, automatic suppression lists, and `List-Unsubscribe` / one-click headers. It costs about nothing at SurveyBeat's volume ($0.35 per 1,000 after 3,000 a month).

+The risks are beta status, an unpublished starting daily quota, no documented dedicated-IP or IP-pool option, a transactional-only policy, and the sending domain must be on Cloudflare DNS. Recommendation: build on Cloudflare, behind an `EmailSender` domain interface, and keep **Postmark** (or Resend) as the named fallback. Decide go or no-go with a seed-inbox deliverability test and a quota check before the first external customer.
+## 1. Status and availability

+- **Public beta since 2026-04-16.** "Email Sending is now in public beta. Send transactional emails directly from Workers (`env.EMAIL.send()`) or the REST API." It joined Email Routing under the name "Cloudflare Email Service". <https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-04-16-email-sending-public-beta/>
+- Private beta was announced 2025-09-25. <https://blog.cloudflare.com/email-service/>

+- The overview page still says beta, with "features and APIs may change before general availability". Arbitrary-recipient sending requires Workers Paid. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/>
+- No GA announcement appears in the product changelog. Its latest entry is dated 2026-09-25 (page updated Oct 15, 2026). <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/changelog/>
+- Changes since the public beta that matter here:
+  - 2026-05-28: display names on all address fields.
+  - 2026-06-08: authenticated SMTP on `smtp.mx.cloudflare.net:465`, also beta.
+  - 2026-07-15: Email Sending events published to Queues.
+  - 2026-07-17: message preview in the Activity log, kept about 7 days.
+  - 2026-09-25: suppressions can be scoped to one sending domain, and automatic bounce and complaint suppressions now use that scope.

+- **Transactional only.** The FAQ asks "Can I use Email Service for marketing emails?" and answers "No. Email Service supports transactional email only." [Oct 15, 2026] <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/faq/>. Cloudflare gives no definition. AWS defines transactional as "sent on a one-to-one basis unique to each recipient usually triggered by a user action" (<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/request-production-access.html>). Invitations and reminders for a pulse the organization set up should qualify: each one is unique to the person, carries a personal token, and is sent to employees of the customer. Confirm this with Cloudflare during the limit-increase request.
+## 2. API from a Worker
+Source: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/api/send-emails/workers-api/>
+- Binding: `"send_email": [{ "name": "EMAIL" }]`. Bindings can be restricted to allowed senders and recipients. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/configuration/send-bindings/>
+- `env.EMAIL.send({ to, from, subject, html?, text?, cc?, bcc?, replyTo?, attachments?, headers? })` returns `Promise<{ messageId }>`. Addresses can be `string` or `{ email, name }`.

+- No API key is needed inside the Worker, because the binding is the credential. Outside Workers there is a REST API (`POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/send`, with an API token) and SMTP. All three share one pipeline and one set of limits. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/api/send-emails/rest-api/>
+- Errors are thrown as `Error` with a `code`. The ones SurveyBeat must map to typed Effect errors are:
+  - `E_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and `E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: retry later through the Queue.
+  - `E_RECIPIENT_SUPPRESSED`: permanent. Show it in the lead's view (SPEC §7, "Failed sends show up in the lead's view with the reason").
+  - `E_DELIVERY_FAILED`, `E_SENDER_NOT_VERIFIED`, `E_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`, and the `E_HEADER_*` validation codes.
+- `send()` accepting the message is not delivery. Delivery outcome arrives asynchronously as an event (§5).
+- Local dev: `wrangler dev` simulates sending. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/observability/local-development/sending/>

+- Alchemy (SPEC §6.1 IaC) has a `Cloudflare.Email.SendEmail` binding descriptor (`allowedSenderAddresses`, …) and a `SendingSubdomain` resource. <https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/email>, <https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/email/send-and-receive>. Its docs do **not** show a resource for the Queues event subscription on Email Sending events. That subscription may need a custom Alchemy resource or an API call in the deploy, to keep the "no dashboard changes" rule.
+## 3. Volume limits
+Source: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/limits/> [Oct 30, 2026]
+| Limit | Value |

+| Daily quota | **Not published.** "New accounts start with a conservative daily quota and scale up over time based on your sending behavior, deliverability rates, and account standing." Increases go through a Limit Increase Request Form. |
+| Per-second rate | Not published. `E_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` exists. |
+| Recipients per message | 50 (to + cc + bcc). SurveyBeat sends one message per person anyway, because every Invitation carries its own token. |
+| Message size | 25 MiB including attachments |
+| Custom headers | 16 KB total; max 20 allowlisted non-`X-` headers; values ≤ 2,048 bytes |
+| Sending domains per zone | 30 (routing and sending combined) |
+| Before a domain is onboarded | Only verified destination addresses can receive mail |

+**What this means for SurveyBeat.** The quota is per account, and a "Monday 9:00 local time" round makes the send bursty. Before launch, file the limit-increase request with an expected peak per day. The Workflow that sends invitations in batches must treat the two limit errors as retryable, using Queue delay or backoff, and must not drop sends silently (SPEC §7).
+## 4. Domain setup: SPF, DKIM, DMARC

+Sources: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/get-started/send-emails/>, <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/concepts/email-authentication/>, <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/postmaster/>, <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/configuration/subdomains/> [Oct 15, 2026]

+- **Requires Cloudflare DNS**: "You must be using Cloudflare DNS to use Email Service." Alchemy's `SendingSubdomain` docs mention fetching the records for zones not on Cloudflare DNS. That conflicts with Cloudflare's page, so treat Cloudflare's statement as authoritative.
+- Onboarding a sending domain (apex or subdomain) adds these records:
+  - MX records on `cf-bounce.<domain>`, for the bounce return path.
+  - SPF `TXT cf-bounce.<domain> "v=spf1 include:_spf.mx.cloudflare.net ~all"`. SPF sits on the bounce subdomain, so SPF alignment with the From domain is relaxed (organizational domain).
+  - DKIM at `cf-bounce._domainkey.<domain>`. Cloudflare generates and manages the keys.
+  - DMARC at `_dmarc.<domain>`. The doc example is `p=quarantine`, and the doc advises starting at `p=none`.
+- Outbound mail is always SPF- and DKIM-signed, and ARC-signed as well. `List-Unsubscribe` is always included in the DKIM signature.
+- Each subdomain is a separate sending domain. Cloudflare recommends separate subdomains for different mail types. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/concepts/deliverability/>

+- Suggested setup: send from `notify.surveybeat.<tld>` (or similar), keeping the apex free for people mail. Use a separate subdomain per environment (staging vs production) so preview stages never touch production reputation.

+- Gmail's rules for bulk senders (5,000+ per day) are SPF, DKIM and DMARC, From aligned with SPF or DKIM, spam rate below 0.30% (target 0.10%), and one-click unsubscribe for marketing or subscribed mail. Cloudflare's automatic records meet the authentication part. <https://support.google.com/a/answer/81126>
+## 5. Bounces, complaints, suppression

+- **Events to a Queue** (since 2026-07-15): `message.delivered`, `message.deferred`, `message.bounced` (permanent, or retries exhausted), `message.failed` (internal or non-SMTP error), `message.rejected` (policy: suppression, validation, spam), `message.complained` (feedback loop). Each subscription covers one sending domain. The payload has `messageId`, `recipient`, `delivery.status`, the SMTP codes, and a `bounce.type`/`classification`. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/event-subscriptions/> [Oct 15, 2026]
+  - This fits SPEC §6.2 directly: a Queue consumer Worker joins `messageId` to the Invitation and records the failure reason for the lead's view. There are no webhooks to verify.
+- **Automatic suppression**, scoped to the sending domain (2026-09-25):
+  - Complaint: no expiration.
+  - Hard bounce for a nonexistent mailbox or domain, or a hard bounce that persists: no expiration.
+  - Other hard bounce: 7 days.
+  - Soft bounce: 24 hours.
+  Manual entries can be added through a REST API (`/accounts/{id}/email/sending/suppressions`). <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/concepts/suppressions/> [Sep 25, 2026]
+- **Drop suppressed recipients** is off by default, so `send()` throws `E_RECIPIENT_SUPPRESSED`. Keep it off: a loud failure is what SPEC §7 asks for.

+- Hard bounces are not retried. Soft bounces retry with exponential backoff. Cloudflare's targets are delivery above 95%, hard bounce below 2%, and complaints below 0.1%. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/concepts/deliverability/>
+- An example shows how to sync app recipient records after bounces and complaints. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/examples/email-sending/sync-recipient-records/>
+## 6. Deliverability and reputation

+- Cloudflare says it runs managed infrastructure "optimized for deliverability". It publishes outbound ranges in `_spf.mx.cloudflare.net` (example `ip4:104.30.0.0/20`), IPv6 support, PTR records, and RBL monitoring. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/postmaster/>

+- Not documented: dedicated IPs, separate IP pools for transactional mail, or any public inbox-placement figures. Reputation is effectively shared with every other Email Service sender, and the product is 7 months into public beta. This is the main unknown, and only a test settles it (see Recommendation).

+- No open or click tracking is documented, and Cloudflare does not rewrite links. The deliverability page advises linking only to your own domain, and avoiding redirects and shorteners. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/concepts/deliverability/>
+  - This is good for one-tap links.
+  - It also means the "open rates" in SPEC §6.2 (Analytics Engine) cannot come from the provider. SurveyBeat would need its own pixel, which is a privacy call. "Answered" is a better metric anyway.
+- Support during the beta runs through the community forum and Discord. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/postmaster/>
+## 7. Cost

+- Workers Paid: **3,000 emails a month included, then $0.35 per 1,000**. Sends to verified destination addresses are free. [Jun 9, 2026] <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/pricing/>

+- Example: an organization of 500 people on a weekly pulse sends about 1 invite, up to 2 reminders and a few lead notices per round. That is roughly 5–7k emails a month, or about $1–1.50 a month above the included amount.
+## 8. One-tap links and List-Unsubscribe

+**List-Unsubscribe is supported.** `List-Unsubscribe`, `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, `List-Id`, `Precedence`, `Auto-Submitted` and any `X-` header are allowlisted. <https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/headers/>
+- `List-Unsubscribe` needs angle-bracketed URIs, and plain `http:` is rejected.
+- `List-Unsubscribe-Post` must be exactly `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` and requires an HTTPS URI (RFC 8058).
+- A request containing any disallowed header is rejected as a whole.
+- `Message-ID`, `Feedback-ID`, `Return-Path`, `Date` and `DKIM-Signature` are platform-controlled. `In-Reply-To` and `References` can be set.
+Suggestions for SurveyBeat:

+- Put a one-click `List-Unsubscribe` on invitations and reminders. Point it at a Worker endpoint that accepts an unauthenticated `POST` carrying a signed token, and turns off reminders (or that pulse) for that person. This matches SPEC §5.1, "A member can turn reminders off". Do **not** implement it as a Cloudflare suppression. An account-scoped suppression would also block results notices and future invitations, and the person would not see the effect in-app.
+- Use `List-Id` per pulse so clients can group and filter. Use `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated` for notices.
+**One-tap links survive transport.** Cloudflare does not wrap links (above), so the rating links arrive unchanged. The receiving side is the constraint:

+- Microsoft Defender Safe Links states that "URLs are scanned prior to message delivery" and that unknown URLs "are detonated asynchronously in the background". It also rewrites links to `*.safelinks.protection.outlook.com` unless the tenant turns that off. <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/safe-links-about> [ms.date 2026-10-14]
+What follows for the design (this is our inference, not Cloudflare's text):
+- A `GET` on a rating link must **not** record an answer by itself. A scanner that follows all five rating links would otherwise submit an answer, or overwrite it with the last value fetched.

+- Let the `GET` render the small answer page with the value preselected. Record the answer with a `POST` from that page, triggered on load by JS or by one tap on "Confirm". Scanners that fetch without running JS then record nothing.
+- The token lives in the URL, so the logging rules in SPEC §5.3 apply to the link-landing request as well.
+## 9. Fallbacks
+What each one needs from a Worker. All of them work with `fetch` alone, and none needs a Node SMTP library.
+| | Cloudflare Email Service | Postmark | Resend | Amazon SES |

+| Send API | Worker binding `env.EMAIL.send()`, no secret | HTTPS `POST /email` with `X-Postmark-Server-Token` | HTTPS `POST /emails` with Bearer API key | SES v2 HTTPS API, **SigV4-signed** (for example the `aws4fetch` library in a Worker); IAM keys as secrets |

+| Bounce and complaint feed | Queue event subscription (no public endpoint) | Webhooks; **no HMAC**, secured by basic auth in the URL plus an IP allowlist; retries 5xx/408/429 with backoff; dedupe on `MessageID` <https://postmarkapp.com/developer/webhooks/webhooks-overview> | Webhooks signed with Svix (`svix-id`, `svix-timestamp`, `svix-signature`; verify on the raw body) <https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/webhooks/verify-webhooks-requests> | SNS topic to an HTTPS subscription (verify SNS message signatures, confirm the subscription), or event publishing through configuration sets to SNS or EventBridge. A feed is **mandatory** <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/monitor-sending-activity-using-notifications-sns.html> |

+| Onboarding friction | Domain must be on Cloudflare DNS; unknown starting quota | Account approval; DKIM plus Return-Path CNAME | DNS records; free tier limited to 100/day | **Sandbox**: verified recipients only, 200 per 24h, 1 per second, until production access is granted (initial response within 96h) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/request-production-access.html> |

+| Price (Nov 2026) | 3k/month included, then $0.35 per 1k | Free 100/month; Basic $15 for 10k, then $1.80 per 1k; Pro $16.50 for 10k, then $1.30 per 1k; dedicated IP $50/month at 300k+ per month <https://postmarkapp.com/pricing> | Free 3k/month (100/day); Pro $20 for 50k, then $0.90 per 1k; dedicated IP $30/month on Scale <https://resend.com/pricing> | $0.10 per 1k (à la carte); dedicated IP $24.95/month; VDM $0.07 per 1k <https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/> |

+| Fit with SPEC | Native; no extra vendor | Transactional-only product with separate transactional and broadcast streams; strong deliverability focus | Best developer experience; signed webhooks | Cheapest at scale, but adds an AWS account, IAM and SNS. SPEC §6 keeps compute and data off other clouds, and this adds a third platform |

+**Ranking for the fallback.** Postmark is first: the product is transactional-only and its reputation is built on that. Resend is second: signed webhooks and a free tier that covers staging. SES comes last: it is cheap, but brings the most integration work and a sandbox wait.
+**Whatever is chosen, keep it swappable:**
+- Define one `EmailSender` Effect service in the domain, with a Cloudflare adapter and, later, an HTTP adapter.
+- Define one `DeliveryEvent` schema. Cloudflare Queue events and vendor webhooks are both parsed into it at the boundary.
+- Unsubscribe and reminder preferences live in SurveyBeat, not in the provider. Switching providers then changes no product behavior.
+## Recommendation for the SPEC §6.1 decision
+1. Use **Cloudflare Email Service** as the primary sender for Release 1. It meets every functional need in SPEC §5.1, §5.8 and §7.
+2. Record **Postmark** as the fallback, triggered by any of the following:
+   1. Seed tests land invitations in spam or junk at Gmail, Outlook.com or a Microsoft 365 tenant, and authentication is correct.
+   2. The granted daily quota is below the projected peak day after a limit request.
+   3. Cloudflare rules SurveyBeat's invitations or reminders out of "transactional".
+   4. A breaking beta API change lands without a migration path.
+3. Before the first external customer:
+   - File the limit-increase request.
+   - Onboard a dedicated sending subdomain per stage.
+   - Set DMARC to `p=none` with `rua` reporting, then tighten it.
+   - Wire the Queue event subscription.
+   - Run a seed-inbox test of an invitation with one-tap links and `List-Unsubscribe`.
+## Open points
+- Size of the starting daily quota: not public, ask Cloudflare.
+- GA date and SLA: none announced as of 2026-11-07.
+- Alchemy support for Email Sending event subscriptions: not documented. Check, or write a small custom resource.
+- Whether Cloudflare will offer dedicated IPs or pools for transactional mail: not documented.
+# Durable Objects (SQLite), Workflows and Cron Triggers: guarantees and limits

+Research for issue #5 (map #1). Collected 2026-11-07 from developers.cloudflare.com. Each source lists the "Last updated" date the page showed on that day. Limits are for the **Workers Paid** plan unless the text says otherwise.
+## Answer in brief

+- **Storage is not the constraint.** A SQLite-backed Durable Object holds 10 GB. 5,000 People answering weekly for 5 years, with 7 Answers per Submission, measured at **0.64 GB with integer keys** and **3.15 GB with UUID text keys** (a 100% response rate, with invitations, participation records and three secondary indexes included). SPEC §6.2 calls this "well under" the limit. That holds with integer keys. With UUID keys the data uses about a third of the limit, which is comfortable but not "far away". See [Sizing check](#sizing-check).

+- **Throughput per object is the real ceiling.** Plan for roughly 500 to 1,000 simple requests per second per object, single-threaded. An Organization-wide burst, such as 5,000 one-tap answers in a minute, is about 83 requests per second. That fits.

+- **Insertion order is observable** through SQLite `rowid`. PITR also keeps every write for 30 days, deletes included. Both matter for the anonymity rule in SPEC §4 (see [Privacy implications](#privacy-implications-for-spec-4)).

+- **Every scheduler involved here can run a step twice.** Alarms are at-least-once and can "fire more than once". Workflow steps are retried. Cron Triggers make no documented delivery promise. The idempotency requirement in SPEC §4 and §6.2 is therefore a platform requirement as well as a design goal.

+- **A Workflow per Round fits the limits.** Sleeps last up to 365 days and do not count as steps. Instances that are waiting do not count against the concurrency limit. A Workflow reaches the Organization DO through `this.env` with an ordinary DO stub and RPC.
+## Durable Objects with SQLite storage
+### Limits
+Source: [Durable Objects limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/) (last updated Oct 29, 2026)
+| Limit | Value |
+| Storage per object | **10 GB** (Paid). The Free plan stops at 1 GB with a storage-full error. |
+| Storage per account | Unlimited (Paid), 5 GB (Free) |
+| Max row, string or BLOB | 2 MB |
+| Max columns per table | 100 |
+| Max SQL statement length | 100 KB |
+| Max bound parameters per query | **100** (this caps multi-row `INSERT … VALUES` batches) |
+| CPU per request | 30 s by default, configurable up to 5 min |
+| Requests per second per object | soft limit of 1,000 |
+| Alarm handler wall time | 15 min |
+| Number of objects | unlimited |
+| Classes per account | 500 (Paid) |
+### Throughput
+Source: [Rules of Durable Objects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/best-practices/rules-of-durable-objects/) (last updated Nov 5, 2026)

+- "A single Durable Object can handle approximately 500-1,000 requests per second for simple operations." The page gives about 500 to 750 for moderate processing and 200 to 500 for complex operations.
+- Each object is "single-threaded". Input gates block new events while synchronous JavaScript runs. Output gates hold responses until pending writes are durable.
+- Writes with no `await` between them are "automatically batched into a single atomic implicit transaction".
+- The page's advice when load exceeds this is to shard across objects.

+Implication: heavy analytics queries run on the same thread as answer intake. A long SQL scan during a send burst delays every answer for that Organization. This argues for the optional per-Round DO, or for precomputed Results, at large Organizations.
+### Transactions
+Source: [SQLite storage API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sqlite-storage-api/) (last updated Sep 21, 2026)
+- Each storage method is implicitly wrapped in a transaction. `transactionSync(cb)` rolls back when `cb` throws.
+- `sql.exec()` cannot run `BEGIN TRANSACTION` or `SAVEPOINT`. Use `ctx.storage.transactionSync()` instead.
+- The supported extensions include FTS5 (comment search), JSON and math functions. Writes to virtual tables count as rows written.
+- `databaseSize` returns the current size in bytes, which supports a monitoring alarm well before 10 GB.
+- KV-API data is stored in a hidden table `__cf_kv`. It appears in table listings but cannot be read through SQL.
+- `deleteAll()` is atomic on SQLite. It deletes the alarm too for compatibility dates of 2026-02-24 or later.
+### Alarms

+Sources: [Alarms API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/alarms/) (last updated Apr 21, 2026) and [Rules of Durable Objects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/best-practices/rules-of-durable-objects/) (Nov 5, 2026)
+- **One alarm per object.** A second `setAlarm()` overrides the first. The time is given in milliseconds since the epoch. No precision guarantee is documented.

+- "Guaranteed at-least-once execution". A handler that throws is retried with exponential backoff from 2 s, up to 6 retries. `alarmInfo.retryCount` and `alarmInfo.isRetry` are exposed to the handler.
+- Only one `alarm()` runs at a time per object. "In rare cases, alarms may fire more than once." Handlers must be idempotent.
+- Alarms do not repeat. The handler must re-arm. Each `setAlarm()` is billed as one row written ([pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing/), Oct 18, 2026).

+- With one alarm per object, an Organization DO that runs its own scheduling must multiplex: keep a schedule table and set the alarm to the earliest due row. Workflows avoid that work for the Round lifecycle.
+### Point-in-time recovery and backups
+Source: [SQLite storage API, PITR section](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sqlite-storage-api/) (Sep 21, 2026)
+- PITR can restore the object "to any point in time in the past 30 days". It is not available in local development.

+- `getCurrentBookmark()`, `getBookmarkForTime(t)` (t must be within 30 days), then `onNextSessionRestoreBookmark(b)` followed by `ctx.abort()`. The restore returns a bookmark for the state before the recovery, so the restore can be undone.
+- Bookmarks are "lexically comparable": earlier points sort first.
+- PITR restores the **whole object**. There is no per-table or per-row restore.

+- **No managed export or backup to external storage is documented.** The [data security page](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/data-security/) (Apr 21, 2026) covers only encryption at rest (LUKS, keys managed by Cloudflare). Backups older than 30 days, and the R2 backups in SPEC §6.2, need application code: an alarm or Workflow that dumps tables to R2, paged to stay under the CPU limit per request.
+### Are rowids and insertion order observable?

+Cloudflare's docs do not mention `rowid` or `AUTOINCREMENT`. The storage is ordinary SQLite, so SQLite's own rules apply ([SQLite rowid tables](https://www.sqlite.org/rowidtable.html), [WITHOUT ROWID](https://www.sqlite.org/withoutrowid.html)):

+- Every table without `WITHOUT ROWID` has a 64-bit `rowid`, readable with `SELECT rowid`. An `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` column is an alias for it. New rows normally get `max(rowid)+1`, so the **rowid encodes insertion order** even when the declared primary key is random.
+- A plain `SELECT` with no `ORDER BY` usually returns rowid order. Code and exports that omit `ORDER BY` leak insertion order.
+- `WITHOUT ROWID` tables have no rowid. They store rows in primary-key order, so a random key (UUIDv4 or a random blob) makes the physical order independent of insertion time.
+- PITR bookmarks give every write a position in the object's history (see the privacy section below).
+## Workflows
+### Limits

+Source: [Workflows limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/reference/limits/) (last updated Nov 4, 2026) and [changelog, 2026-04-15](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-04-15-workflows-limits-raised/)
+| Limit | Paid |
+| Steps per Workflow | 10,000 by default, configurable up to 25,000. **`step.sleep` does not count.** |
+| Step return value | 1 MiB |
+| Persisted state per instance | 1 GB |
+| Max `step.sleep` | 365 days |
+| Concurrent running instances | 50,000 per account (raised from 10,000 on 2026-04-15). The prose on the limits page still says 10,000, which is stale. |
+| Queued instances per Workflow | 2,000,000 |
+| Instance creation rate | 300/s per account, 100/s per workflow |
+| CPU per step | 30 s by default, configurable up to 5 min. Wall time per step is unlimited. |
+| Subrequests per instance | 10,000, configurable up to 10M |
+| Event payload | 1 MiB |
+| Instance ID | 100 characters, unique per Workflow |
+| Completed instance retention | 7 days by default, up to 30 days |
+| `waitForEvent` default timeout | 24 h ([Workers API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/build/workers-api/), Nov 4, 2026) |

+Waiting instances, which includes sleeping, retry backoff and `waitForEvent`, "do **not** count towards concurrency limits". A waiting instance that resumes while the account is at its concurrency limit is queued. Instances that resume from sleep take priority over newly queued instances ([Sleeping and retrying](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/build/sleeping-and-retrying/), Sep 24, 2026).

+Fit for SurveyBeat: a Round needs roughly 10 to 100 steps (open, invitation batches, reminders, close, compute, notify), well under 10,000. Invitation batches have to respect the 1 MiB return value, so a step should return counts or IDs, not payloads. Return values are persisted Workflow state, so Answers and comments must never pass through them, because Workflow state is outside the Organization DO. One Round per Pulse per week across thousands of Organizations means mostly waiting instances, and those do not count toward concurrency.
+### Retry and idempotency semantics

+Sources: [Rules of Workflows](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/build/rules-of-workflows/) (Oct 15, 2026), [Sleeping and retrying](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/build/sleeping-and-retrying/) (Sep 24, 2026), [Workers API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/build/workers-api/) (Nov 4, 2026)

+- Default step config: `retries: { limit: 5, delay: 10000, backoff: "exponential" }`, `timeout: "10 minutes"`. Throwing `NonRetryableError` fails the instance immediately, after any rollback handlers run.

+- "Because a step might be retried multiple times, your steps should (ideally) be idempotent." A step can partly succeed and then retry, for example after sending 300 of 500 emails. Make each send idempotent with a key held in the DO, such as `(round_id, person_id)` on the invitation row.

+- Step results are persisted, and "step names act as the 'cache key'". Names must be deterministic. Code outside steps can run more than once, and in-memory state can be lost when the instance hibernates. Wrap `Date.now()`, randomness and side effects in steps.
+- The `event` is immutable. Pass data between steps through return values.

+- `create({ id })` **throws** if the ID exists and is still within its retention period. `createBatch` does not throw and reports the duplicate as error `10405`. A deterministic instance ID such as `round-<roundId>` therefore deduplicates creation, but only for 7 to 30 days after the instance completes. The DO must stay the source of truth for whether a Round exists.
+- Restarting an instance from a given step reuses the cached results of all earlier steps.
+- Status values: `queued`, `running`, `paused`, `errored`, `terminated`, `complete`, `waiting`, `waitingForPause`, `unknown`.
+### How a Workflow talks to a Durable Object

+- A `WorkflowEntrypoint` reads its bindings through `this.env` ([Workers API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/build/workers-api/); [Bindings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/)). With a DO namespace bound, a step calls `this.env.ORG.getByName(orgId).someMethod()` over RPC ([DO namespace](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/namespace/)).

+- The other direction: a DO holds a Workflow binding and calls `create()`, or `sendEvent()` to wake a `waitForEvent` (for example "lead closed the Round early"). The [durable agents guide](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/get-started/durable-agents/) (Oct 27, 2026) shows this with the Agents SDK (`runWorkflow`, `AgentWorkflow`, `onWorkflowComplete`). Its callbacks to the Agent from a Workflow are labelled "non-durable".

+- No Cloudflare page shows a raw `step.do(() => stub.method())` example. The pattern follows from the pieces above, but it is **not documented as such**. Run it in Miniflare before relying on it. RPC calls are not exactly-once: a step retry calls the DO method again, so DO methods called from steps must be idempotent.
+## Cron Triggers

+Sources: [Cron Triggers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/cron-triggers/) (Oct 17, 2026), [scheduled handler](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/handlers/scheduled/) (Oct 17, 2026), [Workers limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/) (Oct 29, 2026)
+- Five-field cron syntax with Quartz-style extensions (`L`, `W`, `#`). The resolution is **1 minute** (`* * * * *` means "at every minute"). All schedules run in **UTC**.

+- 250 Cron Triggers per account (Paid). CPU time is 30 s for schedules under 1 hour and 15 min for schedules of 1 hour or more. Wall time is 15 min per invocation. Subrequests are capped at 10,000 per invocation.
+- A schedule change can take up to 15 minutes to propagate.
+- `controller.scheduledTime` gives the intended fire time. It works as a natural idempotency key, for example "create rounds due before `scheduledTime`".

+- **Delivery guarantee: none documented.** The Cron Triggers and scheduled-handler pages state no at-least-once, at-most-once, retry or missed-run behaviour. The only first-party hint is the [Containers cron example](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/examples/cron/), which says it does not "guarantee exactly-once execution" and advises idempotent tasks. Design for zero, one or several runs per slot. The hourly "create next Round" job must therefore (a) be idempotent, for example with a unique `(pulse_id, scheduled_open_at)` in the DO, and (b) catch up: create every Round that is due, not only the one for this hour, so a missed tick heals on the next one.
+- Local time zones: because cron is UTC-only, member-local send times belong in the Round's Workflow (`sleepUntil`), not in cron.
+## Sizing check
+Scenario: one Organization DO, 5,000 People, a weekly Round for 5 years, ~7 Answers per Submission, **100% response** (an upper bound).
+- Rounds: 260. Invitations, participation records and Submissions: 1.3M each. Answers: **9.1M**.

+Measured with local SQLite 3 (Python `sqlite3`, after `VACUUM`) at 1/10 scale, 500 People × 260 weeks, then multiplied by 10. The schema: `invitation` (with a unique 43-char token), `participation` (`WITHOUT ROWID`, PK `(round_id, person_id)`), `submission` (indexed on `round_id`), and `answer` (indexes on `submission_id` and `question_version_id`). One of the 7 Answers is a comment of 40 to 400 characters on 30% of Submissions. The script is in this session's scratchpad and can be reproduced from this description.
+| Key style | 1/10 scale | Full scale | Share of 10 GB |
+| `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` | 64 MB | **0.64 GB** | ~6% |
+| UUID text keys (36 chars) | 315 MB | **3.15 GB** | ~32% |
+- Key choice changes the size by a factor of five. UUID text keys and foreign keys dominate. Integer keys, or 16-byte BLOB IDs, keep the 5-year footprint under 1 to 1.5 GB.

+- Headroom remains with UUIDs, but extra indexes, an FTS5 index on comments, stored Results, audit logs, or Organizations above 5,000 People (such as 20,000 People weekly with UUIDs, about 12.6 GB) can reach the limit. Track `databaseSize` and set an alert threshold, for example 5 GB.

+- Write billing over 5 years: each Answer costs about 3 rows written (row plus two indexes), which comes to roughly 30M rows. Spread over 60 months, that is far inside the 50M rows per month included ([pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing/): "every row update of an index counts as an additional row", per the [SQL API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sqlite-storage-api/)).
+- Burst throughput: 5,000 Answers spread over minutes is tens of requests per second. One object handles that.
+## Privacy implications for SPEC §4
+The spec forbids joining participation records to Submissions in anonymous Rounds, "including indirect joins through timestamps, sequence numbers, insertion order".

+1. **rowid.** If a participation record and a Submission are written in the same request, both rowids increase together. Matching by rank then re-identifies the member. Store anonymous Submissions and Answers in `WITHOUT ROWID` tables with random primary keys, never `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` or `AUTOINCREMENT`. Never rely on default `SELECT` order. Alternatively, buffer anonymous Submissions and write them in a shuffled batch, which also helps against timing.

+2. **Same-transaction writes.** Writing the participation record and the Submission in one implicit transaction is the natural way to reject a double submission, and it puts both writes at the same instant in the PITR log. The DO API exposes no per-row history, but anyone who can restore bookmarks can step through history write by write and correlate the two. Treat PITR as able to rebuild the join, and limit who can trigger a restore.
+3. **PITR retention.** Data deleted or scrubbed stays recoverable through PITR for 30 days. That window must appear in the privacy notice and in the data-deletion SLA.
+4. **Workflow state and logs.** Step return values and instance logs are kept for up to 30 days outside the DO. They must never contain Answers or anything that links a person to a Submission.
+## Open points to verify in code
+- Run `step.do(() => doStub.method())` from a Workflow in Miniflare and confirm the retry behaviour.
+- Confirm that the Cloudflare SQLite build exposes `rowid` and accepts `WITHOUT ROWID`. Both are standard SQLite, but Cloudflare's docs do not say.
+- Watch the Workflows limits page for the 10,000 versus 50,000 concurrency text being fixed.
+# Effect HTTP API on Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, and Workflows
+Research for issue #9 (map #1). Researched on 2026-11-07. Throwaway branch, never merged.

+Question: how mature is running Effect, and the HttpApi module (declare the API once, derive the server and a typed client), on Workers, Durable Objects (DOs) and Workflows? SPEC §6.1 fixes Effect, Effect Schema and the HttpApi module. §6.3 requires the domain package to run in plain Node tests.
+## Verdict
+- **Target `effect@4.1.2`** (npm `latest`, published 2026-11-02). Pin every `@effect/*` package to the same version. Effect 4 shipped as 4.0.0 on 2026-10-01 and is an LTS line. Do not start on 3.x.

+- **Workers run the HttpApi module.** `HttpRouter.toWebHandler` is the first-party adapter, and its own API docs carry Cloudflare-specific instructions. A real HttpApi Worker bundles to about 86 KiB gzip and starts in about 55–60 ms of local CPU, against a 1 s limit (my measurements below).

+- **First-party coverage stops at HTTP and SQL.** Effect ships `@effect/sql-d1` and `@effect/sql-sqlite-do`. It ships nothing for DO classes, Workflow entrypoints, Queues or bindings. You either write a thin bridge yourself, or use Alchemy v2 (`alchemy@2.0.0-beta.85`), which is Effect-native and already covers Workers, DOs, Workflows, D1, KV and Queues. SPEC already fixes Alchemy as the infrastructure tool.

+- **Maturity risk is real but bounded.** Every module involved (`effect/http`, `effect/http-api`, `effect/sql`, `effect/workflow`, `effect/schema/Model`, and all `@effect/sql-*` drivers) is tagged `@stability unstable`. That tag allows breaking changes in minor releases. Several Workers-specific bugs were fixed in Sept–Oct 2026, and one fix for request scopes is still open. Pin exact versions and read changelogs before you bump.
+## 1. Effect version and what changed in v4
+| Fact | Source |
+| `effect` dist-tags: `latest: 4.1.2`, `prev: 3.22.4`. 4.0.0 published 2026-10-01, 4.1.0 on 2026-10-29, 4.1.2 on 2026-11-02 | `npm view effect dist-tags time` |

+| "Effect 4.x is a long-term support (LTS) release, with at least three years of bug and security fixes." Bug fixes until Sept 2029 or one year after 5.0, whichever is later | `effect@4.1.2` README; https://effect.website/blog/releases/effect/40 |

+| v4 development moved from `Effect-TS/effect-smol` (now archived, "Effect V4 Has Moved") into `Effect-TS/effect` `main`. v3 lives on the `v3` branch | https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect-smol README |
+| Minimal program: 3.x 35.6 kB vs 4.x 7.1 kB (min+gzip). Throughput 6.4× higher, 86 % less memory per fiber | https://effect.website/blog/releases/effect/40 |
+| Requires TypeScript ≥ 5.9 and `strict`. Node ≥ 22.19 when running on Node | `effect@4.1.2` README |
+What changed for the platform packages (https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/main/MIGRATION.md):

+- **`@effect/platform`, `@effect/rpc`, `@effect/cluster`, `@effect/sql` and others were merged into `effect`.** HTTP is now `effect/http` and HttpApi is now `effect/http-api`. SQL is `effect/sql`, workflows are `effect/workflow`, and so on. `@effect/platform` stays on its v3 line (`0.97.x`). Do not install it with v4.
+- **Lockstep versioning.** Every remaining package (`@effect/platform-*`, `@effect/sql-*`, `@effect/ai-*`, `@effect/vitest`, `@effect/opentelemetry`) shares one version with `effect`.

+- **Unstable module paths lost their `unstable` segment.** Use `effect/http`, not `effect/unstable/http`, and no compatibility exports remain. The modules are still `@stability unstable`, which means "new features in patch releases and breaking changes in minor releases". The migration guide also says "Moving these modules does not stabilize their APIs." The unstable list includes `http`, `http-api`, `rpc`, `schema` (sub-modules such as `Model`), `sql` and `workflow`. Every module in packages other than `effect` is unstable too.

+- Core renames that affect every file: `Context.Tag` → `Context.Service`, `Schema.TaggedError` keeps its name, `catch*` combinators were renamed, and `Runtime<R>` was removed. The links are in MIGRATION.md.
+- There is no `@effect/platform-cloudflare` and no `@effect/cloudflare` package (both 404 on npm). Workers use the platform-neutral `effect/http` directly.
+## 2. Running HttpApi on Workers
+### The adapter

+v3's `HttpApp.toWebHandler` / `HttpApiBuilder.toWebHandler` became `HttpRouter.toWebHandler(appLayer, options)` in v4. It returns `{ handler, dispose }`, where `handler(request, context?)` returns a `Promise<Response>`. Its JSDoc in `effect@4.1.2` (`dist/http/HttpRouter.d.ts`) has a Cloudflare section:

+> On Cloudflare Workers, build the handler at module scope: fibers started inside `fetch` capture that request's async context. Layer construction must not require request-time I/O; bindings are available from `cloudflare:workers` via its `env` export. … For shared fibers, provide a sync scheduler to both layers and requests …
+The recommended shape, which I verified (see §4):
+import { Context, Layer, Scheduler } from "effect"
+import { HttpRouter, HttpServer } from "effect/http"
+import { HttpApiBuilder } from "effect/http-api"
+const SyncScheduler = Layer.succeed(Scheduler.Scheduler, new Scheduler.MixedScheduler("sync"))
+const App = HttpApiBuilder.layer(Api).pipe(
+  Layer.provide(Handlers),
+  Layer.provide(HttpServer.layerServices),
+  Layer.provideMerge(SyncScheduler)
+const { handler } = HttpRouter.toWebHandler(App, { disableLogger: true }) // module scope
+export default {
+  fetch: (req: Request, env: Env) => handler(req, Context.make(CfEnv, env))

+The layer is built when `toWebHandler` is called, not inside the first request. This fixes v3 bug #6319, in which an aborted first request hung the isolate with error 1101 (closed 2026-10-21): https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/issues/6319
+### Typed client

+The client comes from the same declaration: `HttpApiClient.make(Api, { baseUrl, transformClient })` over `FetchHttpClient.layer`. This is shown in `effect/ai-docs/src/51_http-server/10_basics.ts` inside the published package. Renames and schema changes are type-checked end to end. Keep the `Api` declaration in its own module (or package) so that server code stays out of the client bundle. The Effect docs say this explicitly in the same file.
+### Providing bindings (env) as layers, per request

+The `handler`'s second argument is a `Context.Context<ReqR>`. `ReqR` holds whatever services the handlers still require after the app layer is built. The type checker forces you to pass it when it is not `never`. So the clean way to provide Cloudflare bindings per request is:
+1. Declare a `Context.Service` per binding, or one `CfEnv` service. Domain code depends on a domain interface (for example `RoundRepository`), never on `CfEnv`.
+2. Leave those services unprovided in the app layer, and pass `Context.make(CfEnv, env)` (plus `ExecutionContext` if needed) on every call.

+The alternative is `import { env } from "cloudflare:workers"` at module scope, which allows building the layers at module scope. Cloudflare permits reading `env` (vars, secrets, creating DO stubs) at global scope. It does not permit I/O there: no KV, no stub method calls, no fetch (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/). Layers may capture binding handles but must not call them during construction.
+### Workers-specific pitfalls (all from Effect-TS/effect issues)
+| Issue | Status | Consequence for us |

+| [#9025](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/issues/9025) A long-lived fiber hangs once the request that scheduled its next turn has ended | Closed 2026-10-11 by documenting the limits ([PR #9033](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/9033)). The runtime fix [#9032](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/9032) was closed unmerged | Use `MixedScheduler("sync")`. Do not keep background fibers (forkScoped daemons, queue pollers) shared across requests. Put long work in Queues, Workflows or a DO alarm |

+| [#8038](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/issues/8038) `Effect.fn` builds an `Error` per definition at module load, which cost up to 400 ms of startup CPU with 1,600 definitions in a large module | Fixed by [PR #8114](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/8114) (2026-09-07): no capture when `Error.stackTraceLimit === 0` | Set `Error.stackTraceLimit = 0` at the top of the Worker entry if startup grows, which trades away definition-site stack frames. Prefer many small modules |

+| [#9543](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/issues/9543) `FinalizationRegistry` in `HttpClient` throws "Disallowed operation called within global scope" | Closed 2026-10-19 | Fixed in 4.1.x. Shows that outbound `HttpClient` on workerd was only recently hardened |

+| [#6006](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/issues/6006) / [#5987](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/issues/5987) `withTransaction` sent `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`, which DO SQLite forbids | Closed Oct 2026. The 4.1.2 driver now uses `storage.transaction()` | Transactions in DOs work on ≥ 4.1 (see §5) |

+| [#10364](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/issues/10364) `HttpEffect.toHandled` cannot accept a caller-owned request scope, so work handed to `waitUntil` cannot keep request resources open | **Open** (opened by Alchemy maintainers) | Do not use request-scoped resources inside `ctx.waitUntil` work. Telemetry flushing needs care |

+Other v4 notes: `McpServer.layerHttpRequestScoped` exists for serverless hosts (https://effect.website/docs/v4/api/effect/ai/McpServer). Older RPC msgpack used `new Function`, which Workers forbid. That was fixed by moving to msgpackr 1.11.10 (This Week in Effect, 2026-04-24: https://effect.website/blog/this-week-in-effect/2026/04/24/).
+## 3. Durable Objects and Workflows
+### Plain Effect (no Alchemy)
+Effect has no DO or Workflow integration, so you write the bridge. It is small:

+- **Durable Object.** In the constructor, build a `ManagedRuntime` (or a `toWebHandler`) from a layer that closes over `ctx.storage`, with `SqliteClient.layer({ storage: ctx.storage })` and the domain repositories. Run migrations inside `ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile(() => runtime.runPromise(SqliteMigrator.run(...)))`. Each RPC method or `fetch` calls `runtime.runPromise(program)`. The rules in §2 apply here too: build at construction, use the sync scheduler, and no fibers that outlive a request (alarms are the supported way to keep work going).

+- **Workflow.** `class RoundWorkflow extends WorkflowEntrypoint { async run(event, step) { ... } }`. Each `step.do(name, () => runtime.runPromise(effect))` runs one idempotent Effect. Workflow durability (replay, retries, `step.sleep`) stays with Cloudflare. Effect supplies typed errors and services inside each step. Encode step results with Schema, because step outputs must be serializable.

+- `effect/workflow` (Workflow, Activity, DurableClock, DurableDeferred) is an engine-agnostic durable workflow API. The core ships only an in-memory engine and the cluster engine. It has no Cloudflare engine (`effect@4.1.2` `dist/workflow/WorkflowEngine.d.ts`).
+### Alchemy v2: Effect-native Cloudflare runtime

+`alchemy@2.0.0-beta.85` and `@alchemy.run/cloudflare@2.0.0-beta.85` (2026-11-02) have a peer dependency on `effect ^4.1.0`. They define Workers, DOs and Workflows as Effect classes, with bindings resolved as Effect services (https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy, `packages/cloudflare/src/Workers`, `.../Workflows`):

+- `Cloudflare.Worker<Api>()("Api", { main: import.meta.url }, Effect.gen(...))` returns `{ fetch: Effect }`. The init Effect pulls bindings (`yield* Cloudflare.D1.QueryDatabase(Db)`, `yield* Cloudflare.KV.ReadWriteNamespace(KV)`). The demo `demos/effect-prezzy/chapters/02-d1/src/Api.ts` serves an `HttpApiBuilder.layer(ShortyApi)` this way, through `HttpRouter.toHttpEffect`.

+- `Cloudflare.DurableObject<Users>()("Users", Effect.gen(...))` returns typed RPC methods. Callers use `users.getByName(id).listUsers()` (`examples/cloudflare-durable-object-sql`). Migrations come from `Cloudflare.SqlMigrations`.

+- `Cloudflare.Workflow<NotifyWorkflow>()("Notifier", ...)` with `Cloudflare.Workflows.task("name", effect, { retries, timeout, rollback })` wraps `step.do` and threads services into each step (`examples/cloudflare-worker/src/NotifyWorkflow.ts`). Alchemy also implements `effect/workflow`'s `WorkflowEngine` on native Workflows (`NativeEngine.ts`) and on Durable Objects (`DurableObjectEngine.ts`).
+- Alchemy files Workers-runtime bugs upstream and fixes them, for example #10364 above and [alchemy#1639](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/pull/1639) (merged 2026-11-04).

+Trade-off: Alchemy's runtime layer reduces the bridge code to almost nothing, and it matches the SPEC's choice of IaC tool. But it is beta (85 betas, a release every 1–2 weeks), so it couples app runtime code to the IaC tool's release cadence. The domain package stays clean either way, because it depends only on `effect`. Decide this in the architecture ticket. Keep adapters thin, so that moving between the plain bridge and Alchemy's runtime only touches the adapters package.
+## 4. Bundle size and cold start (measured)

+I measured this on 2026-11-07 with `effect@4.1.2`, `rolldown@1.2.13` (the bundler Alchemy uses), `esbuild@0.25.10` and `wrangler@4.158.0` on linux. The Worker serves an `HttpApi` with one group, three endpoints (GET list, GET by id with a typed 404 error, POST with a Schema payload) and an env-backed service, set up as in §2. The client calls `HttpApiClient.make(Api)` with `FetchHttpClient`. The scripts are in the scratchpad and are not committed. Rerun them by bundling the snippet in §2.

+| Minimal `Effect.runPromise(Effect.succeed(1))` | 23.5 KB | 8.4 KB | 167 KB (barrel import) / 27 KB (`effect/Effect` import) | 58 KB / 9.9 KB |

+- **Startup.** `wrangler check startup` reported 53.9 / 58.4 / 61.0 ms active startup CPU across three runs for the HttpApi Worker, against 0–10 ms for a hello-world Worker. That is local workerd, and Cloudflare warns production CPUs differ. In Node 26: 37–43 ms module evaluation, about 45–50 ms for the first request (the layer was already built), and about 120–140 µs per warm request.

For the small answer-page entry, either accept that or call the two or three answer endpoints with plain `fetch` plus the shared Schemas. Schema alone is far smaller than the HttpApi client. Measure this when the entry exists.
+## 5. Effect Schema with SQLite (DO `sql` and D1)

+- **`@effect/sql-sqlite-do@4.1.2`**: `SqliteClient.layer({ db?: SqlStorage, storage?: DurableObjectStorage })` provides `SqliteClient` and the generic `SqlClient`. Pass `storage` (not just `db`) to get transactions and migrations. "Transactions use `storage.transaction()` instead of transaction SQL." Nested transactions roll back on their own. Blobs come back as `Uint8Array`, and `updateValues` is unsupported. `SqliteMigrator.run/layer` records applied migrations in `effect_sql_migrations` and is meant to run "during construction" of the DO (package JSDoc, `dist/SqliteClient.d.ts`, `dist/SqliteMigrator.d.ts`).

+- **`@effect/sql-d1@4.1.2`**: `D1Client.layer({ db: D1Database })`. It caches prepared statements and maps failures to `SqlError`. **No transactions, no streaming, no `updateValues`** (package JSDoc). That fits SPEC's small global index, but multi-row invariants need D1 `batch()` or a design that avoids them.

+- **Schema ↔ SQL**: `effect/schema/Model` (`Model.Class` with `select`/`insert`/`update`/`json`/`jsonCreate`/`jsonUpdate` variants) plus `effect/sql` `SqlSchema` and `SqlModel` give one schema per domain type, shared by the API (`User.json` in the HttpApi fixtures) and the database. SPEC §6.1 asks for exactly this. All of it is `@stability unstable`.

+- **DO SQLite limits to design around**: 100 bound parameters per query, 100 KB per statement, 2 MB per row, 100 columns, 10 GB per object on Workers Paid (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/). Effect's own `SqlEventJournal` chunks at 100 parameters for this reason (`effect/src/eventlog/SqlEventJournal.ts`). Bulk inserts must chunk.

+- **DO write-coalescing caveat**: Cloudflare commits writes with no intervening `await` atomically, and `sql.exec()` is synchronous (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sqlite-storage-api/). Effect's async scheduler can put a macrotask between two statements, so use `withTransaction` explicitly for multi-statement invariants rather than relying on coalescing.
+## 6. Testing with swapped layers in plain Node
+- `@effect/vitest@4.1.2` provides `it.effect` and `layer(TestLayer)("suite", (it) => ...)`.

+- `effect/http-api` `HttpApiTest.groups(Api, ["users"])` builds a typed client wired directly to the handlers, with no server and no network, "using the same request encoding, routing, and response decoding as a real server". The published example (`ai-docs/src/51_http-server/20_testing.ts`) swaps `Users.layerMemory` in for the SQL-backed layer and swaps auth middleware per test. This is exactly the plain-Node domain/API testing that SPEC §6.3 asks for.
+- Because `toWebHandler` returns a plain `(Request) => Promise<Response>`, the same Worker entry can also be smoke-tested in Node with `new Request(...)`. I did this in §4.
+- Adapter tests (DO SQLite, D1, Workflows) still need workerd: `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` or Alchemy's local dev. `cloudflare:workers` `withEnv` overrides imported `env` in tests.
+## 7. Examples in the wild

+- **Alchemy v2** examples and demos (first-party, maintained, Effect 4): `examples/cloudflare-effect-sql-d1`, `examples/cloudflare-durable-object-sql`, `examples/cloudflare-worker` (Worker + DO + Workflow + Queue + KV), `examples/cloudflare-federated-api` (HttpApi), `demos/effect-prezzy` (HttpApi + D1 + Queues chapters). https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/tree/main/examples
+- **danieljvdm/effect-cf**: "Effect-native primitives for Cloudflare Workers and bindings", Effect ^4.1, 116 stars, active (pushed 2026-10-29). https://github.com/danieljvdm/effect-cf
+- **gjermundgaraba/effect-actions PR #51**: Effect RPC served from Durable Objects over hibernating WebSockets. https://github.com/gjermundgaraba/effect-actions/pull/51
+- **deracs/create-effect-project**: Effect v4 scaffolder with a Cloudflare Worker template for HTTP or RPC. https://github.com/deracs/create-effect-project
